# Ball carrier - design notes (generated by ball_carrier.py)

Payload: 30 x 40 mm balls = 81 g. Printed parts: 123 g (at 100 %, thin walls print solid). Robot estimate: 110 g. Total 314 g.

## Capacity
Balls dropped one by one into the lowest free spot (gravity tilted 8 deg): 33 fit fully below a 115 mm wall, so 30 have margin. Bin inside: 192 x 140 mm.

## Stability and traction
CG of robot + full bin: x = 68 mm (drive axle at 0), z = 77 mm.
Load on the drive wheels: 53 % (front skid at x = 144).
Side tip-over at a_lat = 0.65 g -> max 0.98 m/s on a 150 mm radius curve, 1.38 m/s on 300 mm.

## Discharge
Open face: the whole front (140 x 115 mm = 3.5 D wide, open to the top) falls away, so no arch can form (arching needs a roofed outlet narrower than ~4-5 D).
Floor 8 deg on 2 mm rails: rolling resistance of a ball is < 1 deg, so every ball rolls out; the pile above collapses as the front empties (repose ~25 deg).

## Gate and trigger
Ball bed on the gate (Rankine K = 0.41, bulk density 48 kg/m3, fill 111 mm): 6 N.mm static; with down-slope weight and 0.5 g braking 28 N.mm.
Spur foot on the tongue (6.7 mm from the hinge): 0.85 N static, 4.13 N design.
Release force = mu x load = 0.26-1.24 N; robot push at stall ~5.8 N -> 5x margin. Stroke 12 mm; blade sticks out 16 mm ahead of the arm tips.
Trigger stays put while driving: friction 0.26 N vs its inertia at 1 g 0.026 N.
Tongue bending at design load: 9.4 MPa (PLA ~50 MPa).

## Printing
Diamond-truss walls: 45 deg edges need no supports, triangulated for stiffness, 13 mm inscribed opening so a 40 mm ball sinks 1.0 mm < 1.2 mm wall.
Bin prints floor down, gate inner face down, frames flat, trigger tongue down, pins standing.

## Assumptions (change at the top of ball_carrier.py)
Balls 40 mm / 2.7 g; tower rim 50 mm with an opening wider than 140 mm; chassis underside 22 mm above the floor.
